title: Move "Introduction to ASE databases" tutorial to sphinx-gallery examples
body:
Move "Introduction to ASE databases" to examples/deltacodesdft sphinx gallery (See issues: #1783, #1756 )


Closes: #1783

author: elisabeth.keller

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
let's make this nonredundant:

```
dbfile = Path('database.db')
dbfile.unlink(missing_ok=True)

...
db = connect(dbfile)
```

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests a concrete code change to make the code non-redundant by using a Path variable for the database file.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: @HannaTuerk How was it, did we find a way to avoid empty READMEs (or decide what to write in them)? :sweat_smile:

comments.author: HannaTuerk
comments.body: Hey, sorry for the late response. This tutorial should be added directly as .py file in `examples/tutorials` so we can avoid having the extra folder subfolders and empty READMEs files.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Raises a concern about empty READMEs and implies a decision or change needs to be made about their content.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Should these snippets be turned into actual code that runs?

(Do we know how to do that also for the preceding shell commands that create the database?)

comments.author: elisabeth.keller
comments.body: The python snippets from the solution.py script are now included and run. The command line commands (at the moment) were not turned into actual code that runs and are just included as comments.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests converting code snippets into actual runnable code, implying a concrete change should be made.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
It's a little bit strange that this particular example is framed as an exercise, whereas the others are true examples.

Opinions on what we should strive for?  (Maybe also @HannaTuerk?)

If we don't have a particularly good way, we can also just leave it like this so we can finish porting the tutorials, which already provides value.

comments.author: HannaTuerk
comments.body:
True, there are a couple of tutorials that are with this example style, I also thought already it might be better to **change all of them to the tutorial style** (idk who would use this as an exercise).
 For now I suggest we add it as it is (an exercise), and I make a note that we should redo the exercises to be tutorials. (unless @elisabeth.keller  you want to do this directly now, would of course also be very nice)

comments.author: elisabeth.keller
comments.body: I changed database.py more into a tutorial style example and incorporated the solution.py file into database.py, see 7b7b15b3.

comments.author: elisabeth.keller
comments.body: Previously GPAW was used as a calculator, we changed this to EMT. Also, instead of computing and storing the `bandgaps` of the materials as a new key value pair, this was simplified to only do the `energy`.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags that the example is inconsistently framed as an exercise vs. a true example, implying it should be reconsidered or made consistent, even though it also acknowledges leaving it as-is is acceptable.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: now that we have a variable `dbfile` for the db file, we should use that variable throughout the file instead of repeating the string.  (Also further below)

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Explicitly requests using the existing `dbfile` variable throughout the file instead of repeating the string literal.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Best to use meaningful variable names: `for structure in structures`, or `for symbol in structures`

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests renaming a loop variable to a more meaningful name — a concrete style/naming change.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Thanks a lot, sorry for nitpicking!

thread.actionability_reasoning: Pure social acknowledgment/thanks with no code change implied.
